clue.text: Above zero, oxygen and radium in frozen state

indicators.note: in a down entry, above puts the whole preceding assembly on top of the zero
in places the two chemical symbols inside the word for frozen

parts.note: frozen means cold
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen
Ra is the chemical symbol for radium
zero looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A description of something chilled below freezing with gases and radioactive metal locked inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Colorado is one of the fifty states of the USA.

clue.text: You after vacated seat? This for a viewing restriction

indicators.note: after places the old word for you behind the emptied seat
vacated means the word seat is emptied of its inside letters, leaving its ends

parts.note: ye is an archaic form of you

explanation.surface: Someone takes your seat once it is free, and it blocks your view of the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A swollen eyelid infection partly closes the eye, so it restricts what one can see.

clue.text: Great military leader, one driven to catch marine up

indicators.note: to catch says the vehicle surrounds the other piece

parts.note: a car is something that is driven

indicators.note: up, in a down entry, reads the word for marine from bottom to top

parts.note: marine means relating to the sea, so the sea stands for it

explanation.surface: A great general who had to be chauffeured to go and catch a marine.
explanation.definitionFit: Julius Caesar was the Roman general famed as one of history's greatest commanders.

clue.text: Figure something happening in outskirts of Sydney

indicators.note: in sets the occurrence inside the outer letters of the city
outskirts of takes only the edge letters of Sydney

parts.note: an event is something that happens

explanation.surface: Something going on in the suburbs of Sydney is pictured as a figure of note.
explanation.definitionFit: Seventy is a number, and a figure is a numeral.

clue.text: Eye from Magdalene, Trinity and Clare — this area?

definitions.text: Eye from Magdalene, Trinity and Clare — this area?

parts.words: Eye from Magdalene, Trinity and Clare — this area?
parts.note: Magdalene, Trinity and Clare are Cambridge colleges whose rear sides face the river, and the stretch of land seen from behind them has this name

explanation.walkthrough: The Backs is the riverside parkland in Cambridge running behind several colleges, including Magdalene, Trinity and Clare; looking from those colleges, you see it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Backs is the name for the grounds behind Cambridge colleges along the river Cam.

clue.text: Burps, one coming up through taste for fine dining

parts.note: burps are wind, or gas

indicators.note: through says the reversed piece runs right through the word for taste

parts.note: to taste is to try

indicators.note: coming up, in a down entry, reads the word for one upward

parts.note: mono is a prefix meaning one

explanation.surface: Belching after a meal as one savours each mouthful at a gourmet restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: Gastronomy is the art and practice of good eating.

clue.text: Discovery — vehicle on which Scott's setting out

indicators.note: on, in a down entry, puts the initial on top of the vehicle
setting out means the start of Scott's, its opening letter

parts.note: a trike is a three-wheeled vehicle

explanation.surface: Captain Scott sets off on a tricycle, mistaking it for his polar ship Discovery.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes Scott's polar ship Discovery, but here a discovery is a find, as in a gold strike.
explanation.definitionFit: A strike is a find of oil or minerals, a discovery.

clue.text: Sweet Spooner's to plunder headquarters

indicators.note: Spooner's says the opening sounds of the two words are swapped

parts.note: to plunder is to loot
a base is a headquarters

explanation.surface: The Reverend Spooner proposing a raid on a command centre.
explanation.definitionFit: A bootlace is a long thin strip of liquorice sold as a confection.

clue.text: See 10
Sweet nothing, passion about right

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring

indicators.note: about says the word for passion goes around the letter for right

parts.note: heat is intensity of feeling, passion

explanation.surface: A tender word, nothing much, and ardour concerning what is right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet nothing' reads as a whispered endearment, but 'Sweet' alone is the definition and 'nothing' gives LOVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Love hearts are heart-shaped fizzy confectionery tablets printed with short messages, a British favourite.

clue.text: Sweet Queen Elizabeth, perhaps, protecting herself, Elizabeth and daughter

indicators.note: protecting means the vessel wraps around the other pieces

parts.note: the Queen Elizabeth is an ocean liner, so an example of a ship
the Queen herself signs as ER, Elizabeth Regina
Bet is a short form of the name Elizabeth

explanation.surface: The Queen guarding herself, another Elizabeth and her daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: A sherbet dip is a British confection of fizzy powder eaten with a lollipop or liquorice stick.

clue.text: See 22
Cassius claims Van Gogh's surgical instrument possibly makes things tidy

indicators.note: claims means the boxer's name takes in the other piece

parts.note: Cassius Clay was Muhammad Ali's birth name
Van Gogh cut off part of his ear, so a whimsical tool for that could be an ear saw

explanation.surface: A boxer seizes the tool Van Gogh used on his ear, which tidies things up.
explanation.definitionFit: To clear away is to remove clutter, leaving a place neat.

clue.text: Done with credit? Then idle

parts.note: on tick is British slang for on credit
something done is over

explanation.surface: Asking whether a deal is settled on account, then lazing about.
explanation.definitionFit: An engine that ticks over runs slowly while idle, out of gear.

clue.text: Doctor meeting fate lacking in reserve

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor

indicators.note: lacking says the word in is removed from the word for fate

parts.note: destiny means fate
taken as written

explanation.surface: A physician confronting a doom that is short on restraint.
explanation.definitionFit: Reserve as a character trait is restraint or modesty about oneself.

clue.text: Work routine going up, strange being in plane

indicators.note: going up, in a down entry, reads the two pieces for work and routine together from bottom to top

parts.note: a job is work
a rut is a dull routine
ET is the film's alien, a strange being

explanation.surface: Daily grind rising, and an odd creature found aboard an aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: A turbojet is a jet aircraft or its engine, so it stands for a plane.

clue.text: Special gift, flower, for support

parts.note: ESP, extrasensory perception, is a special psychic gift
a flower is something that flows, a river; the Ouse is an English river

explanation.surface: A rare present of a bloom offered as backing.
explanation.definitionFit: To espouse a cause is to adopt and back it.

clue.text: Evil in punching nun

indicators.note: punching says the small word goes into the word for nun

parts.note: a nun is a sister
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something wicked in hitting a nun.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinister describes menace or wickedness, as in a sinister motive.

clue.text: Sound of rain at leaving an inscription in what provides the final tribute

indicators.note: an inscription is something written into a surface, so the shortened sound is written into the word for what

parts.note: eh is an exclamation asking what

indicators.note: leaving says the word at departs from the sound of rain

parts.note: pitapat is the light tapping of falling rain
taken as written

explanation.surface: Rain pattering as someone departs, and words carved on a tribute to the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: An epitaph on a gravestone is the last tribute paid to someone who has died.

clue.text: Sweet to speak of brace and bit

indicators.note: to speak of says the word for brace is said aloud, giving a fruit's name

parts.note: a brace is a pair
a drop is a small bit

explanation.surface: A carpenter talking about his drill and its attachment.
explanation.definitionFit: Pear drops are hard British boiled confections with a pear flavour.

clue.text: 'E with oversized head in essence?

parts.note: 'E is the cockney pronunciation of he

indicators.note: in places the letter inside the word for essence

parts.note: the gist is the essence

indicators.note: head takes the first letter of oversized

explanation.surface: A cockney asking whether a bloke is essentially big-headed.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-centred person thinks too much of themselves, as one with an inflated ego.

clue.text: Sweet evidence of bull in china shop?

definitions.meaning: a confection of rice paper filled with sherbet, shaped like a disc

definitions.text: evidence of bull in china shop?
definitions.meaning: a bull rampaging in a crockery shop sends dishes through the air

explanation.definitionFit: Flying saucers are disc-shaped rice-paper sweets, and the phrase literally describes airborne crockery.

clue.text: Weak charge down, uranium dropped

parts.note: a fee is a charge

indicators.note: dropped says the uranium symbol falls out of the word for down

parts.note: feeling down is feeling blue
U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: A price going down after radioactive metal is discarded.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeble and weak are synonyms meaning lacking strength.

clue.text: Bird hosting party let off, as sweet

indicators.note: hosting says the bird contains the party

parts.note: a coot is a waterbird
Lab is short for the British Labour Party

indicators.note: off signals the word let is jumbled

explanation.surface: A bird holding a party lets things go, sweetly.
explanation.definitionFit: Cola bottles are gummy sweets shaped like little bottles and cola-flavoured.

clue.text: See 25
Christian partial to Hindi, ordained

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A Christian with a fondness for an ordained Hindu speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Christian Dior was the French fashion designer, so his first name points to him.

clue.text: Carrying drugs primarily, a suspect not to be trusted popping sweet in mouth

indicators.note: carrying says the rearranged letters hold the extra letter
not to be trusted says the letters of a suspect are unreliable and must be reshuffled
primarily takes the first letter of drugs

explanation.surface: A dodgy suspect smuggling narcotics, with something fizzing in their mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not to be trusted' scrambles A SUSPECT into SPACEUST, which carries D to make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Space Dust was a brand of crackling candy that pops on the tongue.

clue.text: Top bird nursing full stomach

indicators.note: nursing says the bird holds the other piece inside

parts.note: a plover is a wading bird

indicators.note: stomach means the middle letters of full

explanation.surface: A bird feeding a full belly.
